ROLE
You are helping a team of B.Tech students build a Java course project. Build it in phases and STOP after each phase so we can review, run, and confirm before you continue. Do not build everything at once.

PROJECT
CineFlow: a Movie Ticket Reservation System, a JavaFX desktop app for a multiplex.

FIXED TECH STACK (do not substitute or add frameworks)
- Java 21 (JDK 21), Maven
- JavaFX 21.x (build the UI in Java code, NOT FXML; style with one CSS file)
- MySQL 8.x with JDBC (MySQL Connector/J) and PreparedStatement for every query
- NOT allowed: Spring, Spring Boot, Hibernate/JPA, Lombok, Redis, Docker, any ORM
- Password hashing: JDK only (SHA-256 with random salt via MessageDigest and SecureRandom)

WHY THIS STACK
This is graded on a faculty rubric. The top tier ("Outstanding") requires Event Handling + JavaFX + MySQL with rich operations. Full marks need committed features to be FULLY implemented and working. Quality over quantity: do not add features beyond this list.

CODE STYLE RULES (we must explain every line in a viva)
- Beginner-friendly Java: clear names, short methods, comments explaining WHY, no clever tricks, no advanced generics or reflection.
- Use only concepts from a Java course: OOP, collections, exceptions, interfaces, JDBC, JavaFX events.
- try-with-resources for connections, statements, result sets.
- Never concatenate user input into SQL. Always PreparedStatement.
- Packages: model, dao, service, ui, util. DAO classes hold ALL SQL. UI classes never contain SQL.
- DB credentials in db.properties (not hard-coded); include db.properties.example.
- Show errors in user-friendly alert dialogs, never silent failures.
- Keep each module in its own package or classes so five teammates can work in parallel without merge conflicts.

DATABASE (create schema.sql and seed_data.sql)
Tables: users, movies, screens, seats, showtimes, bookings, booking_seats, seat_holds, payments.
- users: id, username (unique), password_hash, salt, full_name, email, role (ADMIN or CUSTOMER), active
- movies: id, title, genre, language, duration_minutes, rating, description, release_date, active
- screens: id, name, total_rows, seats_per_row
- seats: id, screen_id (FK), row_label, seat_number, seat_type (REGULAR or PREMIUM); unique (screen_id, row_label, seat_number)
- showtimes: id, movie_id (FK), screen_id (FK), start_time, price_regular, price_premium; no overlapping showtimes on the same screen (validate in code)
- bookings: id, user_id (FK), showtime_id (FK), booking_time, total_amount, status (CONFIRMED, CANCELLED)
- booking_seats: id, booking_id (FK), showtime_id (FK), seat_id (FK), price; UNIQUE (showtime_id, seat_id) so double booking is impossible even if code fails
- seat_holds: id, showtime_id (FK), seat_id (FK), user_id (FK), held_until
- payments: id, booking_id (FK), method (CASH, UPI, CARD), amount, status (PAID, REFUNDED), paid_at
Seed: one ADMIN, two CUSTOMERS, 2 screens with generated seats, about 8 movies, about 12 showtimes across the next 5 days, and about 25 past bookings across several dates so reports have data.

COMMITTED FEATURES (all must be fully working)
1. Login and registration with role-based access. ADMIN: everything. CUSTOMER: browse, book, view and cancel own bookings.
2. Admin: movie management (CRUD, mark active or inactive).
3. Admin: screen and showtime management (create showtimes, block overlaps on the same screen).
4. Customer: browse movies and showtimes, search and filter by title, genre, language and date.
5. Seat map: a grid of seat buttons for a showtime. Colors: available, selected, held by someone else, booked. Premium seats look different. Clicking toggles selection; hovering shows seat label and price; total updates live.
6. Seat holds: when the customer proceeds to payment, selected seats are inserted into seat_holds with a 5-minute expiry. A countdown label shows time left. A JavaFX Timeline releases expired holds (and the seat map refreshes). Expired holds are also ignored by queries.
7. Booking: payment dialog (simulated: choose method, confirm). Confirming runs ONE JDBC TRANSACTION: re-check seats with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, insert booking, booking_seats, payment, delete holds. If any seat is taken or anything fails, ROLLBACK and show a clear message.
8. My Bookings: list own bookings with details; show a ticket summary dialog.
9. Cancellation: customer can cancel a booking if the show has not started. One transaction: set booking CANCELLED, mark payment REFUNDED, free the seats (remove booking_seats rows).
10. Admin booking management: view all bookings with filters (date range, movie, status, user) using JOINs.
11. Reports (Admin): total revenue, bookings today, bar chart of revenue for last 7 days, pie chart of top movies by tickets sold, occupancy percentage per showtime (aggregate queries with GROUP BY).
12. CSV export of bookings and reports.
13. Input validation everywhere (empty fields, duplicate username, invalid numbers, past showtimes, overlapping showtimes).

EVENT HANDLING (the rubric grades this, so make it visible and varied)
- ActionEvent on buttons throughout.
- MouseEvent: seat click, seat hover (enter and exit), double-click a table row to edit.
- KeyEvent: Enter on login, Delete shortcut on admin tables.
- Search-as-you-type using a text property listener.
- Listeners on seat selection that recalculate the total.
- Timeline/countdown for hold expiry.
- Confirmation dialog on window close (setOnCloseRequest).
- Selection listeners on tables and ComboBoxes (movie, date).
Add a short comment above each handler naming the event type.

PHASES (stop and wait for my "continue" after each)
Phase 1: Maven project (pom.xml with JavaFX and MySQL dependencies, javafx-maven-plugin so "mvn javafx:run" works), package structure, schema.sql, seed_data.sql, db.properties handling, DBConnection class, and a main window that opens and shows "Database connected". Give exact commands to run and verify.
Phase 2: Models, UserDAO, hashing utility, login and registration screens, role-based navigation.
Phase 3: Admin movie, screen and showtime management.
Phase 4: Customer browsing, search and filter, and the seat map (selection, hover, colors) without saving yet.
Phase 5: Seat holds with countdown, payment dialog, booking transaction with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE and rollback, ticket dialog.
Phase 6: My Bookings, cancellation with refund transaction, admin booking management with JOIN filters.
Phase 7: Reports with charts, CSV export.
Phase 8: Validation pass, CSS polish, error handling review, README with setup steps, and a list of main concepts used (for viva prep).

AFTER EACH PHASE, give us:
1. What was built, in 3-5 plain sentences.
2. The exact command to run it and what we should see.
3. The 3 most important concepts in this phase we should be able to explain in a viva.
4. Any assumptions you made.
Then ask whether to continue.
